status: Unreviewed full working proof of degree-slope conditional M0, with actual original-reference construction route

steps.title: Actual curve and fixed paths
steps.text: Let B be complete algebraically closed nontrivially real-valued, D/B an actual smooth connected projective curve, A an ample Q-line bundle of RAW degree a>0, and M=dA integral with a nonzero global section S0. Fix finitely many actual typeII points z_i. Choose ONCE a compact semistable skeleton Gamma containing them and let D0=max_{i,j} d_Gamma(z_i,z_j), retaining all cycles; D0=0 for one point. This actual skeleton and D0 do not depend on any later FS metric. No arbitrary graph realization or inverse curvature premise is used.

steps.title: Finite valued-extension completion proof
steps.text: For a valued finite field extension E/E0 of degree delta, let H be the completion of E and F the completion of E0. The isometric inclusion E0->H extends to F->H. An E0-basis of E spans an F-vector space W in H of dimension<=delta. W is closed because finite-dimensional normed spaces over a complete valued field are complete. Here is an elementary proof: induct on a basis; the previous span W' is complete and closed, so for v outside it c=inf_{w in W'}|v-w|>0. For any b, |w+bv|>=|b|c, and |w|<=max(|w+bv|,|b||v|). These estimates inductively give equivalence with the maximum-coordinate norm, hence completeness. W contains dense E, so H=W and [H:F]<=delta. Lift any independent residue classes over F-tilde to norm1 elements in H. A nontrivial F-linear relation, divided by a coefficient of maximum absolute value, would reduce to a nontrivial residue relation. Therefore [H-tilde:F-tilde]<=[H:F]<=delta. No discreteness, spherical completeness, defectlessness or equality in the fundamental inequality is assumed.

steps.title: Pole bound for actual section quotients
steps.text: For t!=0 in H0(D,kM), set f=t/S0^k. A constant f has zero slope. Otherwise f extends to a finite flat nonconstant morphism D->P1: use the whole Stacks53.2.1-4. Its degree delta=[B(D):B(f)] is the degree of the pole divisor, which is the pullback of infinity; see whole Stacks33.44.11 and33.44.9. The pole divisor is coefficientwise bounded by k div(S0). Consequently delta<=k deg(M)=kd a. All degrees are RAW; cancellations reduce the bound.

steps.title: Annular slope from a residue-field index
steps.text: Refine the skeleton for D minus the finite zeros and poles of f, preserving Gamma with its original metric (BPR3.13). On an open annulus for each edge piece, f is a genuine analytic unit. On a closed strict subannulus BPR2.2(1) gives f=c T^q(1+g), q in Z, |g|_sup<1. Thus log|f| has slope q up to orientation in logarithmic length. For rho in |B*| inside the interval, set tau=T/b, |b|=rho. At its actual Gauss point x, H(x)-tilde=B-tilde(tau), while H(x) is the completion of the honest B(D), since x has generic scheme support. If q!=0 the residue of f/(c b^q) is tau^q, hence transcendental. Every polynomial in f therefore has its exact Gauss value: distinct powers have independent residues after maximal-coefficient normalization. The completed subfield B(f) has residue B-tilde(tau^q), of degree |q| in B-tilde(tau). S2 with E=B(D), E0=B(f) gives |q|<=delta. The q=0 case has zero slope. Density of |B*| radii and continuity extend the Lipschitz estimate to entire closed pieces, including typeIII points. This proves the global slope bound without a total-curvature identity.

steps.title: Integrate on fixed paths with cycles
steps.text: The finite divisor can cause subdivisions and attached rays, but BPR3.13 leaves the fixed Gamma isometric to its original realization. Summing |slope log|f||<=delta along a shortest finite path in Gamma gives |log|f(z_i)|-log|f(z_j)||<=delta d_Gamma(z_i,z_j). All endpoint values are finite because the points have generic support. Cycles remain; no tree replacement or singular terminal convention is introduced.

steps.title: Entire pure FS maximum and denominator
steps.text: Clear a common denominator and amplify a finite defining section family so any genuine pureFS metric psi on A is represented by t_l!=0 in H0(D,kM), with real constant weights beta_l. Raising each defining section to the same power preserves the metric and basepoint-free condition. In the rational S0/d frame its weight is w_psi=(1/(kd)) max_l(log|t_l/S0^k|+beta_l). Divide the ENTIRE expression, including every constant weight, by kd. By S3-S5 each term has Lipschitz constant<=kd a on Gamma. Their finite maximum has that same constant. Thus |w_psi(z_i)-w_psi(z_j)|<=a d_Gamma(z_i,z_j), uniformly in k, every section family and all real weights. Delete zero sections; constant quotients are harmless.

steps.title: Conditional all-dimensional M0
steps.text:
Let X/C be actual smooth geometrically integral projective of dimension n>=2 over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued characteristic/residue characteristic0 C. Let L be ample Q with RAW V=(L^n), M=dL an actual fixed very ample embedding by S0,...,SN, and theta=FS(S0,...,SN)/d with zero weights. Suppose a finite norming set y_i has generic support, |S_l/S0(y_i)|<=1, maximal residue transcendence degree n, and coordinate residues generating a subfield of transcendence degree n. Suppose ONE fixed actual common coefficient-Gauss curve D/B and typeII lifts z_i preserve EVERY original rational function value, as intended in the whole UNREVIEWED native243 Lemmas7/8, Proposition9, Theorem10. Its actual L_D degree is a=d^(n-1)V. Choose D0 once as S1. This whole incidence construction is a dependency to reconstruct, not a caller grant.
For genuine original pureFS psi normalized by sup_X(psi-theta)=0, norming gives a y_j with value0. The rational S0/d-frame weight of theta is0 at EVERY y_i and z_i because S0 appears in the list and all coordinate ratios have norm<=1. Restriction of each nonzero original section t_l to D is nonzero: its nonzero generic value at y_i is preserved at z_i. Apply S6 to the same section family restricted to D. Therefore |(psi-theta)(y_i)-(psi-theta)(y_j)|<=a d_Gamma(z_i,z_j), and -aD0<=(psi-theta)(y_i)<=0 for every i and ALL original pureFS metrics. The actual curve and paths are fixed before psi. This is a complete working proof of M0 under exactly these point/curve hypotheses, not an unconditional original solution.

steps.title: Finite atomic pure FS dual estimate
steps.text: For nu=V sum_i c_i delta_yi, c_i>=0, sum c_i=1, and E_theta(0)=0 in RAW mass V, monotonicity gives E_theta(u)<=0 for u=psi-theta<=0. S7 gives -int u dnu<=VaD0. Hence 0<=sup_{pureFS u}(E_theta(u)-int u dnu)<=VaD0. One atom is allowed. Extending this to all actual E1, intrinsic target integrability, unit bounds and coercivity requires the ENTIRE continuous-net/energy proofs of243 or a complete accepted criterion with matching hypotheses; it is not automatically an all-E1 operator statement.

steps.title: Preserve an original-field reference
steps.text: Over original K of characteristic/residue characteristic0, choose an original sufficiently high M=dL with a finite very ample embedding basis over K, high enough for all243 negative-power cohomology hypotheses by actual field Serre duality/vanishing. Freeze this embedding and theta. Use an actual complete algebraically closed nontrivial extension C for geometry. A trivially valued K needs an actual chosen nontrivial extension and correctly scoped descent. Original K-section families form a subset of C-section families. Do not use GM A.7 on the transcendental coefficient-Gauss extension.

steps.title: Actual same-reference projective closure and finite normalization
steps.text: Take mathcalX0, the schematic closure of X_C in P^N_{C-circle} under that SAME original embedding. The finite-type affine rings inject into their generic fibre and are torsion-free over the valuation ring, hence flat. BE4.5 supplies finite presentation. Normalize mathcalX0 in X_C; BE4.20 over algebraically closed C gives a FINITE model morphism p:mathcalX->mathcalX0 with REDUCED special fibre. The generic fibre remains identical X_C because it is already normal. Set mathcalM=p^*O(1), whose actual generic bundle is M_C. Finite/quasi-affine pullback of an ample bundle is ample by the general forward Stacks29.38.7(2). Do not apply Noetherian two-way30.17.2 to C-circle. The original pulled-back embedding sections still generate mathcalM, so max_i |S_i|=1 in every actual model frame. Its metric is EXACTLY the original zero-weight pureFS theta_C. No vertical metric change, separate carrier algebraization or mass-only identification is used.

steps.title: Maximal residual initial points: exact remaining upstream application
steps.text: Apply BE4.8/6.3 and GM A.1-A.5 to actual affine formal charts of this reduced model. Points over generic residual components form the finite norming Shilov set and are divisorial in the strictly analytic definition. GM A.5 gives s(y_i)=dim_yi X_C^an=n, because the actual carrier is smooth n-dimensional. The residual component field injects into H(y_i)-tilde by the reduction-kernel definition. Maximal residual dimension forces generic scheme support on integral X_C. The reverse implication of printed GM A.5 cites Poineau2013 Lemma4.4, while A.3 cites GRW2017 Proposition2.12; their original published sources have just been retrieved and still need whole pertinent proof reading. This exact application is pending. A one-point fibre alone is not a residue-field isomorphism. The stronger whole-field equality is not required by243's coordinate SUBFIELD hypothesis.

steps.title: One original-field chart nonzero at every component
steps.text: Because original S_i generate mathcalM, not all vanish at any of the finitely many residual generic points. Bad coefficient vectors making sum lambda_i S_i vanish at one such point form a proper linear kernel over C-tilde. Its intersection with the original K-tilde vector space is a proper K-tilde subspace: some standard basis vector has nonzero image. K-tilde is infinite in residue characteristic0; choose a coefficient vector outside the finite union of these proper subspaces and lift its coefficients to K-circle. At least one is a unit; complete it to an elementary invertible basis change over K-circle and call the resulting combination S0. Both matrices are integral, so the zero-weight FS reference stays EXACTLY the same. S0 has norm1 at every y_i, and every new original ratio g_l=S_l/S0 has norm<=1 there. The whole new embedding family remains defined over K.

steps.title: Residual coordinate subfield from actual finite projection
steps.text: On S0!=0 in mathcalX0_s, the original g_l generate the coordinate algebra of the actual closed projective-space chart image. The finite morphism mathcalX_s->mathcalX0_s maps every residual component generically finitely onto its image. Once the complete initial-point/dimension application P3 supplies dimension n for the relevant residual components, their function fields are finite over the subfield generated by these coordinate residues. That subfield has transcendence degree n, and it need not equal all of H(y_i)-tilde. Do not infer purity of every fibre component solely from the degree n of a Hilbert polynomial. This actual finite closed-chart image is the precise route to243's residual-coordinate premise.

steps.title: Norming every original FS metric
steps.text: BE6.3(i) on mathcalM^k gives sup_X |t|_{kd theta}=max_i |t(y_i)|_{kd theta} for every algebraic section t of kM. Constant weights and finite maxima commute with these suprema; align all denominators first. Thus sup_X(psi-theta)=max_i(psi-theta)(y_i) for every genuine pureFS psi. This supplies only finite-set norming; S7 supplies individual lower bounds. Scalar extension of theta is identified by its exact original FS family, not by equality of arbitrary lattice norms under extension.

steps.title: Finish whole actual common-curve construction
steps.text: After P1-P6, reconstruct ALL of native243 Lemmas7/8, Proposition9 and Theorem10: full residual independence of every generic hyperplane coefficient, actual proper geometrically smooth integral complete-intersection curve and its explicit cohomology, honest generic curve-valued field before completion, residue transcendence degree1 and value-group calculation for all lifts, then the separate algebraic-completion typeII argument. The native paper is unreviewed; none of these statements is a grant. With this SINGLE fixed actual curve, S1-S8 produce M0 without a new inverse curve-curvature construction. The fact that every original rational-function value survives also prevents any original nonzero section from vanishing identically on D.
